except SystemExit: pass
print("  the classifier's own rules, read as a constraint:\n")
print("    definition = 2  requires METH and INP")
print("    definition = 1  requires METH and NOT INP")
print("    inputs     = 1  requires INP")
print("    -> definition = 1 and inputs = 1 cannot both hold. **The two axes are not independent.**\n")
src=open('The Method 1.3.md',encoding='utf-8').read()
pop=defaultdict(set)
for par in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', src):
    if not ni.NUM.findall(par): continue
    q,c=ni.classify(par); pop[q].add(c)
occ=set()
for v in pop.values(): occ|=v
viol=[c for c in occ if c[0]==1 and c[1]==1]
print(f"  occupied cells violating it: {len(viol)}   (a constraint refuted by its own extent would be dead)")
def R(X):
    vals=[sorted({c[i] for c in X}) for i in range(3)]
    def env(a,b):
        m={}
        for c in X: m[c[b]]=max(m.get(c[b],-99),c[a])
        z=-99;o={}
        for t in sorted(m): z=max(z,m[t]); o[t]=z
        return o
    phi={(a,b):env(a,b) for a in range(3) for b in range(3) if a!=b}
    return {x for x in product(*vals) if all(x[a]<=phi[(a,b)][x[b]] for a in range(3) for b in range(3) if a!=b)}
ok=lambda x: not(x[0]==1 and x[1]==1)
print(f"\n  {'fibre':14s} {'E before':>9s} {'E after':>8s}")
b=a=0
for q in sorted(pop):
    X={tuple(c) for c in pop[q]}
    eb=len(R(X))-len(X); ea=len({x for x in R(X) if ok(x)})-len(X)
    b+=eb; a+=ea
    print(f"  {q:14s} {eb:9d} {ea:8d}")
print(f"  {'all':14s} {b:9d} {a:8d}")
print(f"\n  the constraint removes {b-a} of {b} cells, and refutes nothing the book prints.")

 either by a number that belongs there or by a constraint the coordinates are missing.

 **Refuted twice.** That a recomputed number must carry a stated definition, and that it must carry at
 least enumerated inputs. Both are principled and **both are contradicted by cells the book already
 occupies** — four numbers recorded as recomputed while their definition is only asserted, three while
 their inputs are only named. A constraint refuted by its own extent is dead, and those seven cells are
 what the failure leaves behind: **a recomputation whose definition is not stated is not checkable.**

 from F.3's own assignment rules rather than judged. *Definition = stated* is assigned exactly when a

§12.11.3.1 divides bounds by provenance: **a bound from a law is stable; a bound from an extent moves with the extent.** E(G) is an extent quantity, so of course it moves. The index was asserting an extent measure as though it were a law.

Three instances in three turns turned out to be one category, and the sweep found where the line falls.

**§30.1.4.1 — Which of this book's numbers hold still.** Measured across three states of the book:

| figure | before intake | before compression | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| E(Λ) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| \|Λ\| | 976 | 976 | 976 |
| generators \|J(Λ)\| | 17 | 17 | 17 |
| surplus, bits per cell | 7.07 | 7.07 | 7.07 |
| elements of Appendix D | forty | **forty-eight** | forty-eight |
| E over the numbers index | 33 | **21** | **23** |
| E(Q), unfibred | 1 | 1 | **4** |

> **Every figure about Λ holds. Every figure about the book moves.**

Not a coincidence and not a defect. **Λ is a fixed mathematical object; the book is a text that changes.** A measurement of Λ is a measurement; a measurement of the book is a reading taken at a moment. §12.11.3.1 sorts bounds into law-derived and extent-derived — and the same division sorts the book's own numbers, with the line falling exactly at the boundary between the object and the work about it.

**§30.1.4's fifty-five is 48 today**, and that's stated rather than quietly corrected.

**What a reader gets from it:** every figure in Parts II and III checks against the construction and will agree forever. Every figure the book states about *itself* is true of a named state. Two are recomputed at build. **Three more are still asserted and shouldn't be** — that's named as outstanding rather than claimed done.

Entry 373. **213 pages, 94,902 words.** Register 165–373, 168 entries. All twenty audits pass.

**The three routes aren't equivalent.** By the *law* is best where one exists — §F.3.3 replaces a count with the constraint that generates it, which cannot go stale. By the *stable structure* where no law exists — the nine combinations that hold in every state, against a count that read five values in one session. By *computation at build* is weakest and necessary where the quantity is genuinely a reading.

**I had broken it one turn earlier.** §E.1.3 removed E(Q) and supplied only the fibred statement — the unfibred count had **no representation at all** until I extended the press just now. A rule stated after the act it governs is a rule found by breaking it, and the entry says so.

26:    register 165–374, 16,197 words, withdrawal ratio 0.272

E(G) moved from 23 to 22 while I wrote this section — which is the phenomenon, demonstrating itself in the build log.

Two failures on the way, both mine and both caught: I numbered the new protocol 2.20 where 2.20 already existed, and then placed it by hand instead of by position. SEQUENCE caught both.

import re
p='The Method 1.3.md'; s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
m=re.search(r'^### 2\.20 [^\n]*',s,re.M); anchor=m.group(0)
new = """### 2.20 A figure removed must have its data represented another way
 §F.3.3 and §E.1.3 remove two counts because a figure computed from the book cannot be printed as
 prose. **Removal is not a repair on its own.** A stale number is wrong; a missing number is not
 therefore right, and deleting one without replacing what it carried loses the reader something the
 book knew.

    **Any figure withdrawn must have its data represented another way** — by the law that generates
    it, by the stable structure beneath it, or by a computation the artefact performs. The
    withdrawal and the replacement are one act.

 **Three representations are available and they are not equivalent.**

 **By the law.** Best where one exists. §F.3.3 replaces a count with the constraint that generates it —
 *definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated* — which cannot go stale because it is a fact about
 the assignment rules rather than the text.

 **By the stable structure.** Where no law is available but the shape holds still. §F.3.3 names the
 nine combinations admitted and absent in every state of the book, against a count that read five
 different values in one session; §E.1.3 asserts E(Q) = 0 under its fibration, which has held at five
 different item totals.

 **By computation at build.** The weakest, and necessary where the quantity is genuinely a reading. The
 press prints E(G), the open count, E(Q) unfibred, the register's span and the withdrawal ratio on
 every build. **These are readouts and are marked as such** — a number the artefact computes about
 itself is evidence of a state, not a claim about the work.

 **And the rule caught its author immediately.** §E.1.3 removed E(Q) and supplied only the fibred
 statement; the unfibred count had no representation at all until the press was extended to compute it,
 one turn later. **A rule stated after the act it governs is a rule found by breaking it.**
 Register 374.

""" + anchor
assert s.count(anchor)==1
s=s.replace(anchor,new)
i=s.index('### 26.7.7'); j=s.index('### 26.8')
blk=s[i:j].rstrip('\n')
e=""" 374. **A protocol at §2.20: any figure withdrawn must have its data represented another way** — by the
 law that generates it, by the stable structure beneath it, or by a computation the artefact performs,
 and the withdrawal and the replacement are one act. Stated at the author's instruction, and **it
 caught me at once**: §E.1.3 had removed E(Q) one turn earlier and supplied only the fibred statement,
 leaving the unfibred count with no representation at all. The press now computes E(G), the open item
 count, E(Q) unfibred, the register's span and the withdrawal ratio at every build, and prints them as
 readouts rather than claims. **A rule stated after the act it governs is a rule found by breaking it.**

"""
s=s[:i]+blk+'\n\n'+e+s[j:]
s=re.sub(r'([Tt])hree hundred and seventy-three(?! corrections)', lambda m:m.group(1)+'hree hundred and seventy-four', s)
s=s.replace('three hundred and seventy-three corrections','three hundred and seventy-four corrections')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
seq=[m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r'^### (2\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)',s,re.M)]
key=lambda t:[int(v) for v in t.split('.')[1:]]
print("chapter 2 monotone:",seq==sorted(seq,key=key),"| duplicates:",[x for x in set(seq) if seq.count(x)>1] or "none")

**§2.21 — A figure removed must have its data represented another way.** And it caught me immediately.

> Any figure withdrawn must have its data represented another way — **by the law that generates it, by the stable structure beneath it, or by a computation the artefact performs. The withdrawal and the replacement are one act.**

**The three routes aren't equivalent.** By the *law* is best where one exists — §F.3.3 replaces a count with the constraint that generates it, which cannot go stale. By the *stable structure* where no law exists — the nine combinations that hold in every state, against a count that read five values in one session. By *computation at build* is weakest and necessary where the quantity is genuinely a reading.

**I had broken it one turn earlier.** §E.1.3 removed E(Q) and supplied only the fibred statement — the unfibred count had **no representation at all** until I extended the press just now. A rule stated after the act it governs is a rule found by breaking it, and the entry says so.

**The press now prints five readouts at every build:**

```
F.3:   E(G) = 22, recomputed at build over 6 fibres
E.1.2: 11 open items, E(Q) = 4 unfibred, recomputed at build
26:    register 165–374, 16,197 words, withdrawal ratio 0.272
```

E(G) moved from 23 to 22 while I wrote this section — which is the phenomenon, demonstrating itself in the build log.

Two failures on the way, both mine and both caught: I numbered the new protocol 2.20 where 2.20 already existed, and then placed it by hand instead of by position. SEQUENCE caught both.

  **unusable**, which is a different cost and the one this coordinate names.

 from 17 to 16. That is the third of that count confirmed by a defect rather than proposed, after
 SEQUENCE and PROJECTION.

 **Why the other twenty could not catch it.** ARITHMETIC and ENUMERATION check a number against a
 computation the book performs; SCOPE checks that a figure carries its frame. **All three presuppose
 the input exists in the text.** A result whose input was never printed passes every one of them,
 because there is nothing for them to disagree with — the same shape as PROJECTION's finding that
 correctness and completeness are different failures.

 **First run: nine stated results tested, nine pass** — but only because registers 376 and 377 printed
 the two tables an hour earlier. Run against the book as it stood this morning it would have failed
 twice. Register 379.

assert s.count(anchor)==1
s=s.replace(anchor,new)

 print the data it was computed from. Registers 376 and 377 found the same defect twice in two turns —

 correct and neither checkable. **Its cell was among the seventeen §3.8 had listed as admitted and
 absent**, the third of that count confirmed by a defect rather than proposed; adding it takes
 E(audits) to 16. **The other twenty cannot catch it** because ARITHMETIC, ENUMERATION and SCOPE all
 presuppose the input exists in the text, so a result whose input was never printed gives them nothing
 to disagree with. Nine results tested, nine pass — and only because the two tables were printed an
 hour earlier; against this morning's book it fails twice.

"""
s=s[:i]+blk+'\n\n'+e+s[j:]

    def env(i,j):

        b=-99;o={}

    phi={(i,j):env(i,j) for i in range(D) for j in range(D) if i!=j}
    Rl=step(st,"reconstruct Λ",lambda: len({x for x in product(*vals) if all(x[i]<=phi[(i,j)][x[j]] for i in range(D) for j in range(D) if i!=j)}),budget=60)

    byr=defaultdict(list)

    J=[x for x in L if len([y for y in byr.get(sum(x)-1,[]) if leq(y,x)])==1]
    chk("A.19","|J(Λ)| = 17",len(J),17)

    L13=[c+(Jv,) for c in L12 for Jv in range(max(0,c[11]-1),c[11]+2)]

import re, subprocess, pdfplumber, os
s=open('The Method 1.3.md',encoding='utf-8').read()
P='/mnt/user-data/outputs/The Method 1.3.pdf'
t=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',subprocess.run(['pdftotext',P,'-'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
bad=[]
print("=== STRUCTURE ===")
key=lambda x:[int(v) for v in re.findall(r'\d+',x)]
for c in range(1,31):
    sec=[m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r'^### ('+str(c)+r'\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)',s,re.M)]
    if sec!=sorted(sec,key=key): bad.append(f"ch{c}")
print(f"  chapters 1–30, sections monotone      {'yes' if not bad else bad}")
SECL=re.compile(r'^ ([A-F]\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*) (\S[^\n]{0,70})$')
for x,nx in [('A','B'),('B','C'),('C','D'),('D','E'),('E','F'),('F',None)]:
    i=s.rindex(f'# Appendix {x}')
    Ax=s[i:(s.rindex(f'# Appendix {nx}') if nx else s.rindex('# END MATTER'))]
    q=[m.group(1) for l in Ax.split('\n') if (m:=SECL.match(l)) and not re.search(r'\s{3,}\S',m.group(2))
       and not m.group(2).endswith(('.',',')) and len(m.group(2).split())<=12]
    if q!=sorted(q,key=key): bad.append(f"App{x}")
print(f"  appendices A–F, sections monotone     {'yes' if not any(b.startswith('App') for b in bad) else 'NO'}")
refs=set(re.findall(r'§(\d{1,2}\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)',s))
hd=set(re.findall(r'^### (\d{1,2}\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)',s,re.M))|set(re.findall(r'^\s{0,2}(\d{1,2}\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+[A-ZΛ]',s,re.M))
un=[r for r in refs if r not in hd and int(r.split('.')[0])<=30]
print(f"  § references unresolved               {un or 'none'}")
apr=set(re.findall(r'§?\b([A-F]\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\b',s))
aph=set(re.findall(r'^\s{0,3}([A-F]\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+\S',s,re.M))
print(f"  appendix references unresolved        {sorted(x for x in apr-aph if len(x)<9) or 'none'}")
reg=s[s.rindex('## 26. Withdrawals'):s.rindex('## 27.')]
nums=set()
for m in re.finditer(r'^\s{0,3}((?:\d{3}, )*\d{3})\.\s',reg,re.M):
    nums|={int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d{3}',m.group(1))}
print(f"  register numbers 199–380 absent       {[x for x in range(199,381) if x not in nums] or 'none'}")
print()
print("=== ARTEFACT ===")
pdf=pdfplumber.open(P)
im=sum(1 for l in subprocess.run(['pdfimages','-list',P],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines()[2:] if l.split()[2]=='image')
print(f"  pages {len(pdf.pages)} | figures {im}/32 | stray ** {t.count('**')} | glyphs {'ok' if chr(0xfffd) not in t else 'FAIL'}")
print(f"  source {os.path.getsize('The Method 1.3.md'):,}b | pdf {os.path.getsize(P):,}b")
W=lambda x: len(re.sub(r'[*#`|]','',x).split())
print(f"  words {W(s):,} | register {W(reg):,} ({100*W(reg)/W(s):.1f}%)")
print(f"\nVERIFICATION: {'CLEAN' if not bad and not un else 'ISSUES '+str(bad+un)}")
PYEOF

Both done, and E.3 was worse than "a lot to address."

**E.2 removed.** Eight answered questions, each already carrying the section of the book that holds its answer — the appendix was maintaining the same claim in two places. Replaced by one paragraph naming the eight and their sections, per §2.21: the data is represented by the sections that hold it, and the register carries what each cost. **247 words to 145.**

**And E.3 had drifted badly.** It is subordinate to E.1.2 and the two must list the same items. They didn't:

- **six open items had no entry at all** — G, H, I, M, N, P
- **one entry was an item already answered** — E, the target-spin axis, settled at §12.11.1

That drift opened across the closures of registers 364, 365 and 371, and nothing was watching. Six entries written, one removed, and **audit 15 extended so the pair is compared on every run.** A summary and the thing it summarises maintained separately — §26.7.8's mechanism, seventh instance.

Two of my own errors on the way, both caught: I wrote E.2's heading with two leading spaces and E.3's with none, which took both out of the section list entirely — SEQUENCE saw it. And the register needed re-sorting twice because my first sort covered only half the block.

**216 pages, 97,966 words.** Appendix E at 2,867. Register 165–384, 179 entries. All twenty-one audits pass.

from method_tower import base, terms, phihat
CAPS=[(3,3,1,3,1),(4,4,1,6,1),(4,4,2,6,2),(5,5,2,6,2)]
with State("densities", reset=True) as st:
    def run(cap):
        L=base(cap)
        fmax=cap[4]
        ph={k:phihat(k,fmax) for k in range(0,4*fmax+3)}
        L9=[c+(s,) for c in L for s in range(0,c[6]+1)]
        L10=[c+(v,) for c in L9 for v in range(c[8],c[6]+1)]
        L11=[c+(j,) for c in L10 for j in range(0,ph.get(c[2],0)+1)]
        # exact target-side 2J_c per cell, for the density
        ex=0
        for c in L10:

import re

 answer rather than an opinion. At the build that produced this page: **E(Λ) = 0, E(audits) = 16,
 E(G) = 19, E(Q) = 5 unfibred, E(D) = 4 unfibred — forty-three cells in all.** Three kinds of thing sit
 inside that number, and they are not equally worth doing.

 **Cells that are dominated, and should stay empty.** Register 387 tested the numbers index and found
 ten of eleven admitted cells dominated: for each, a cell the fibre already occupies is at least as
 good on every axis, so filling it adds nothing a reader wants. **E(X) counts what a structure admits,
 not what it should contain** — §6.3's calendar, where E = 7 is the price of keeping January first. The
 same test has not been run on the other three indices, and it should be before any of their cells is
 treated as work.

 **Cells that wait for a defect, and cannot be filled to order.** The sixteen missing audits are of this
 kind. Three of that count have been occupied — SEQUENCE, PROJECTION and INPUT — and **each arrived
 because a defect got past the set, not because a cell was empty.** Register 275 states why: E(audits)
 = 0 was once true and weak, and the set grew when a coordinate was added rather than when audits were
 invented. An audit written to fill a cell would test nothing that has ever gone wrong.

 **Cells that are ordinary work.** Ten open items in Appendix E, of which **eight stop at the same
 requirement — *is it reachable from here*** — a scan not exposed, a file not readable, a literature not
 entered. One waits on a measurement that does not exist, and one is unbounded by nature.

    **So the honest count is not forty-three.** It is: some number of dominated cells that should
    stay empty, sixteen audits that should wait, and **eight fetches that would close eight
    questions.**

 **And two things sit outside all four indices.** §E.1.4 shows the open set cannot express an unclosable
 question — every value of its obstacle column names a route — so the multiverse reading of §27.2.2 and
 the destination coordinate of the temporal mechanisms are not open items and never will be. **They are
 the shape of the question this book cannot pose.** Register 396.

""" + anchor

"""

Yes — and I put the question to the indices rather than answering it myself, which is §30.6.1.

**Forty-three cells stand admitted and absent** — E(Λ) = 0, E(audits) = 16, E(G) = 19, E(Q) = 5, E(D) = 4. **But the count overstates the work by most of its size**, and three different kinds of thing sit inside it.

**Cells that should stay empty.** Register 387's domination test, run on the numbers index, found **ten of eleven cells dominated** — a cell the fibre already occupies is at least as good on every axis. E(X) counts what a structure admits, not what it should contain. **That test has not been run on the other three indices**, and it should be before any of their cells is treated as work.

**Cells that wait for a defect.** The sixteen missing audits. Three of that count have been occupied — SEQUENCE, PROJECTION, INPUT — and **each arrived because something got past the set, not because a cell was empty.** An audit written to fill a cell would test nothing that has ever gone wrong.

**Cells that are ordinary work.** Ten open items, of which **eight stop at the same requirement — *is it reachable from here***: a scan not exposed, a file not readable, a literature not entered.

> **So the honest answer is: some number of dominated cells that should stay empty, sixteen audits that should wait, and eight fetches.**

**And two things sit outside all four indices permanently.** §E.1.4 shows the open set cannot express an unclosable question, so the multiverse reading and the destination coordinate are not open items and never will be.

Writing that tripped audit 13, which was reading the register's historical figures as disagreements — **register 341 and 381 a third time.** The register is exempt from being read as repetition *and* as disagreement, and is not exempt from having its references resolve. Audit 13 now excludes it and watches E(audits) as a third quantity.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The phase closure (register 398).
#
# Work is ordered: FETCH < READ < ANALYSE < REPORT. Each phase is closed before
# the next begins. This is not a pipeline — it is a closure operator, and the
# same one the book applies to Λ.
#
#   extensive   closing only ever adds settled work; nothing already closed is lost
#   monotone    more input closes at least as much as less input did
#   idempotent  re-closing a closed state changes nothing
#
# A REOPEN drops back to the earliest phase the new fact touches and re-closes
# forward. It is legitimate only when a *recorded* fact triggered it — without
# that requirement, "closed until more information arrives" is indistinguishable
# from never closing at all. The register is what makes the operator self-defending.

PHASES = ["fetch", "read", "analyse", "report"]


class Closure:
    """Phase-ordered work with closure semantics, backed by a State."""

    def __init__(self, st):
        self.st = st
        self.done = {p: [] for p in PHASES}
        self.phase = 0
        self.reopens = []

    def at(self):
        return PHASES[self.phase]

    def close(self, phase, items):
        """Settle a phase. Refuses to run out of order."""
        i = PHASES.index(phase)
        if i > self.phase:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"cannot close '{phase}' while '{PHASES[self.phase]}' is open")
        self.done[phase] = sorted(set(self.done[phase]) | set(items))
        if i == self.phase and self.phase < len(PHASES) - 1:
            self.phase += 1
        print(f"  closed {phase}: {len(self.done[phase])} item(s); now at {self.at()}")
        return self.done[phase]

    def reopen(self, phase, fact):
        """Drop back. Legitimate only with a recorded fact; refuses without one."""
        if not fact or not str(fact).strip():
            raise RuntimeError("a reopen needs a recorded fact — refusing")
        i = PHASES.index(phase)
        self.reopens.append((phase, fact))
        self.phase = min(self.phase, i)
        print(f"  reopened at {phase}: {fact}")
        return self.phase

    def snapshot(self):
        return {p: tuple(self.done[p]) for p in PHASES}
'''
if 'class Closure' not in s:
    open(p,'w').write(s+add); print("phase closure added to zeno.py")

The fetch phase can't close because I can't get what's needed, which means nothing downstream can proceed—and that's actually the right constraint here. The discipline is working as it should.

summaries.summary: Discovering inability to retrieve actual file attachments.
Identified inaccessible files; recognized constraint preventing task completion.

content.text:
**Fetch cannot close, so nothing downstream may proceed** — and under §2.20.1 that's the whole answer until it does.

**No conversation named "transitions" exists in this project.** The search returned the same five it always does: *The Method 1*, *indexing without prediction*, *Lattice formalism for electronic occupancy sequencing*, *Lach Elemental Lattice 2026 overview*, and *A theory to explore*. The nearest match is *The Method 1*, whose subtitle is **an index of transitions** — but that's this book's own subtitle, not a separate chat.

**And the harder limit stands regardless of naming.** My conversation tools return **summaries and text excerpts only**. They do not return attachments. Even with the right chat in hand I could recover what was *said* about a file and never the file.

What I did get back is substantive but it's prose, not data — the excerpt on axes 12 and 13, the E1 puncture's four meets all producing the forbidden cell, the Ba I clause (ii) contradiction still unresolved in the companion paper. **All of that is already in the book**, absorbed in earlier sessions.

**So: upload them.** Attach the documents and the fetch phase closes properly, and I'll take them under the four phases — read and inventory, recompute every checkable figure before anything is written, place into the method, register, audit. That's better than recovery would have been, since I'd be working from the artefacts rather than a summary's account of them.

**If you'd rather I keep looking**, give me a distinctive phrase, a result, or a filename from that conversation — a content word from the discussion itself searches far better than a topic label. But if the chat sits outside this project, no search reaches it.

Baseline holds: restore point taken, 102,924 words, register at 400, twenty-one audits green, nothing running.
